description: Add `mo info` command for environment and installation source overview with default, --verbose, and --json output modes

tasks.title: Implement `mo info` command with default output
tasks.description: Add a new `InfoCommands` class following the existing CLI command builder pattern, an `InfoCollector` service that aggregates data from local sources (systemctl, procfs, git, filesystem, HTTP), and register `mo info` as a top-level command in `MohistCliCommands.Build()`. Default output covers: CLI version and binary path, server and runner service status with PID and uptime, resolved source directory with git commit, runner-to-server connectivity, active project with issue counts, and data directory path. All collectors use independent error handling with sentinel fallback values. Cross-platform: full systemd on Linux, graceful degradation on macOS/Windows.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo info` is registered as a top-level command and produces output in <1s under normal conditions
Default output includes CLI version with binary path, server and runner status (active/inactive/not installed) with PID and uptime when running
Each service line includes a source path resolved from systemd unit `WorkingDirectory` with git short SHA and commit subject
Runner line shows connectivity indicator (server ok / server unreachable) when server is running, skipped when not
Project line shows active project name with total and active issue counts via `/api/projects`
Data directory line shows path with total disk usage
Single field failures (service not running, no git repo, missing data dir) display sentinel values (<not running>, <not a git repo>, <unknown>) without blocking other fields
macOS/Windows displays platform notice 'service management not supported on this platform' and degrades gracefully
Command is read-only: no files, services, or configuration are modified on repeated execution
Existing commands (`mo status`, `mo server status`, `mo runner status`) produce identical output before and after this change
Unit tests cover all collector methods with mocked `ICommandExecutor`, each fail-safe scenario, systemd unit parsing fallback chain, and cross-platform degradation
tasks.output: `mo info` default output producing <=10 lines of environment and installation source overview
tasks.notes: Reuse `ICommandExecutor` for systemctl/git/ps. Reuse `MohistCliApi` for HTTP calls. Per-collector timeouts via `CancellationTokenSource` with 2s max. Source path resolution: FragmentPath -> WorkingDirectory -> ExecStart --project -> binary directory fallback chain. Connectivity check uses `/api/projects` endpoint.

tasks.title: Implement `--verbose` output mode
tasks.description: Add `--verbose` flag support to `mo info` that appends supplementary sections below the default output: installed skills list (name, path), git remote origin URL from source directory, opencode runtime info (command, version, available models), relevant environment variables (MOHIST_*, SERVER_URL, RUNNER_ID, MAX_CONCURRENT_WORKFLOWS), OS/arch/.NET/Node versions, runner active capacity, and disk usage breakdown by category (projects, logs, worktrees). Each verbose section is independently collected with fail-safe sentinel fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo info --verbose` appends all supplementary sections below default output with clear section headers
Skills section lists installed skills with name and install path
Git remote section displays origin URL when source directory is a git repo with a remote
Opencode runtime section shows command, version, and available model count
Environment variables section lists MOHIST_*, SERVER_URL, RUNNER_ID, MAX_CONCURRENT_WORKFLOWS values
OS/runtime section shows OS name, architecture, .NET runtime version, and Node.js version
Runner capacity section shows active and maximum concurrent workflow counts
Disk usage section shows breakdown by projects, logs, and worktrees categories
Any verbose field that cannot be read displays `<unknown>` or is omitted without blocking other verbose fields
Unit tests cover each verbose section collector with mocked data sources and fail-safe scenarios
tasks.output: `mo info --verbose` output including all supplementary environment sections
tasks.notes: Skills list uses existing `SkillAssetService.ListVisibleSkills()`. Git remote uses `git -C <path> remote get-url origin`. Opencode runtime info comes from opencode settings API or config file. Disk usage computed per-category with fallback to <unknown> if slow. Node.js version via `node --version`.

tasks.title: Implement `--json` output mode
tasks.description: Add `--json` flag support to `mo info` that serializes all collected information as a single nested JSON object to stdout using `System.Text.Json`. Field names correspond one-to-one with default and verbose output fields. Missing fields are rendered as `null` or sentinel strings. `--json --verbose` includes all verbose sections in the JSON structure.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo info --json` outputs a single valid JSON object to stdout with keys for cli, server, runner, project, and dataDir
Server and runner JSON objects include nested status, source, and git sub-objects
Missing fields are `null` (for absent objects) or sentinel strings (`<not running>`, `<unknown>`) for absent scalar values
`mo info --json --verbose` includes all verbose sections (skills, gitRemote, opencodeRuntime, envVars, osRuntime, capacity, diskUsage) in the JSON object
JSON field names are stable and documented (no renames or removals without breaking change notice)
Unit tests verify JSON structure shape, null handling for missing fields, and combined --json --verbose output
tasks.output: `mo info --json` producing stable machine-readable JSON output
tasks.notes: Use `System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer` with `JsonSerializerOptions { WriteIndented = false }` for compact output. Define a strongly-typed `InfoResult` record to serialize. For `--json --verbose`, verbose sections are included conditionally based on whether the flag is set — the JSON structure is additive, not alternative.
